vision.oneLine: Ind AS 103 tells the buyer of a business how to record what it bought: everything at fair value, with goodwill (or a capital-reserve gain) as the balancing figure.
vision.why: Business combinations feed every consolidation question (Ch 13) and appear on their own in RTPs, MTPs and papers: acquirer identification, contingent consideration, step acquisitions, measurement-period changes and common-control mergers. Indian carve-outs (bargain purchase to capital reserve; Appendix C pooling) are favourites.
vision.marks: about 8 marks an attempt, more inside consolidation questions
sixty: Business combination = control + a business; else it is an asset purchase (no goodwill).
Find the accounting acquirer — it may not be the share issuer (reverse acquisition).
Consideration at fair value; deal costs to P&L; contingent consideration at fair value on day 1.
Recognise all identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value; contingent liabilities that are present obligations too.
Goodwill = consideration + NCI + old stake at FV − net assets; negative → capital reserve.
One-year measurement period for day-1 facts.
Group mergers under common control: pooling at carrying amounts.

askedAs.how: Identify the acquirer and the acquisition date; goodwill and NCI working; contingent consideration classification.
Goodwill/bargain figure, treatment of acquisition costs, measurement-period adjustments.
Journal entries and balance sheet after merger of fellow subsidiaries under pooling.

pitfalls: Taking a bargain purchase gain to profit or loss.
Capitalising due-diligence and legal costs in goodwill.
Using the old carrying amount of a previously held stake.
Fair-valuing assets in a common control merger.
Adjusting goodwill for contingent-consideration changes caused by post-acquisition events.

levels.title: Business combination or asset purchase?
levels.hook: Wrong classification means wrong goodwill, costs and deferred tax.

teach.html: Control (Ind AS 110) and a business (input + substantive process). Outputs are not required.
Optional: if substantially all gross assets sit in one asset or similar group → not a business. Gross assets exclude cash, DTA and goodwill from DTL.

recall.q: Building ₹1,000 cr, cash ₹200 cr, liabilities ₹800 cr; consideration incl. NCI and old stake ₹500 cr. Gross assets for the concentration test (₹ crore)?
A shell company with no activities is a business.
recall.why: No integrated set of activities — no goodwill (SM Example 7).

recall.q: Equipment (FV ₹500 cr) and patent (FV ₹1,000 cr) bought for ₹1,000 cr cash + land (FV ₹400 cr), not a business. Patent recorded at?

twist.q: The building were only 70% of gross assets?
twist.a: Concentration test fails; assess inputs and substantive processes before concluding.

levels.title: Who is the acquirer and when?
levels.hook: Reverse acquisitions and acquisition dates are classic short notes.

teach.html: Whoever obtains control. In share swaps look at post-deal voting, board, management, premium and size.
The share issuer is the accounting acquiree; consideration = shares the real acquirer would have issued × its price.
When control passes — not the appointed date or the date shares are transferred.

recall.q: A issues 2.5 shares for each of B's 60,000 shares; A has 30,000 shares; B's price ₹105. Deemed consideration (₹)?
A's net assets at FV ₹11,00,000. Goodwill (₹)?
Shareholder agreement 1 June, appointed date 1 April, board control 1 July, payment 15 July, shares 1 August. Acquisition date?
recall.why: Control via board on 1 July (SM Example 12).

twist.q: If A's owners kept 80% after the swap?
twist.a: A would be the acquirer — a normal acquisition.

levels.title: Consideration, costs, step acquisitions, contingent consideration
levels.hook: Contingent consideration classification (equity vs liability) is asked repeatedly.

teach.html: Fair value of cash, assets, liabilities to former owners, equity issued and contingent consideration. Deal costs expensed.
Remeasure the old stake to fair value (P&L, or OCI if FVOCI) and include it in goodwill.
Fixed number of own shares → equity, never remeasured. Cash or variable shares → liability, remeasured through P&L for post-acquisition events.

recall.q: Due-diligence fees for the deal are part of goodwill.
Contingent consideration: a fixed number of the acquirer's shares if a profit target is met. Later fair value rises. Treatment?
recall.why: Equity-classified contingent consideration is not remeasured (SM TYK 10).

recall.q: Shares issued 10,00,000 × ₹20 and contingent consideration FV ₹25 lakh. Purchase consideration (₹ lakh)?

twist.q: The target becomes unlikely after six months, cash-settled. Effect?
twist.a: Remeasure the liability; gain in profit or loss; goodwill unchanged (SM Example 14).

levels.title: Recognising and measuring what you bought
levels.hook: Exceptions (contingent liabilities, indemnification, reacquired rights) score easy marks.

teach.html: All identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value, including unrecorded brands and customer lists.
Contingent liabilities: recognise present obligations measurable reliably. Indemnification assets mirror the indemnified item. Reacquired rights over the remaining contract term.
Assembled workforce and contracts under negotiation are subsumed in goodwill.

recall.q: Claim ₹250; seller indemnifies losses above ₹100. Indemnification asset (₹)?
A contingent liability that is a present obligation but not probable is recognised in a business combination if fair value is reliably measurable.
recall.why: Recognition exception — contrary to Ind AS 37 (SM Example 15).

recall.q: Which is subsumed into goodwill?

twist.q: Confidentiality terms prohibit selling the customer list. Recognise it separately?
twist.a: No — it fails the separability criterion; it goes into goodwill (SM Example 17).

levels.title: Goodwill, NCI, bargain purchase and the measurement period
levels.hook: Every consolidation answer starts with this working.

teach.html: Consideration + NCI + old stake (FV) − net assets (FV). NCI at fair value or proportionate share.
Reassess first; then OCI → capital reserve with clear reason, else directly to capital reserve.
Up to one year, for facts existing at acquisition → adjust goodwill retrospectively.

recall.q: Net assets exceed consideration after reassessment, reason clear (forced sale). Gain goes to?
New information within 1 year about a day-1 fact adjusts goodwill.
Maximum measurement period (years)?

twist.a: Measurement period over — treat as an Ind AS 8 error if it existed at acquisition; otherwise a later event in P&L.

levels.title: What is part of the deal: pre-existing relationships, employee payments, share awards

teach.html: Settling pre-existing relationships, paying for future services, reimbursing the acquirer's costs — outside the combination.
Pre-combination portion = measure × served ÷ max(total, original) → consideration; rest → remuneration.

recall.q: Award ₹500; 2 of 5 years served; not replaced. Amount to NCI at acquisition (₹)?
Pre-combination portion ₹100, 95% expected to vest. Amount in consideration (₹)?
Contingent payments forfeited if the seller leaves employment are part of consideration.

twist.q: The same payments continue even if the seller leaves?
twist.a: Indicator of additional consideration rather than remuneration.

levels.title: Common control combinations (pooling)
levels.hook: Indian Appendix C — a near-certain question in group-restructuring scenarios.

teach.html: Same ultimate controller before and after, not transitory.
Carrying amounts; harmonise policies only; restate comparatives; reserves keep their identity; shares at nominal value; difference to a separate capital reserve.

recall.q: In pooling, assets are recorded at?
Prior periods are restated as if the combination occurred from the start of the earliest period presented (or from when common control began).
Pooling steps in order

twist.q: Common control was arranged for two weeks before a sale to an outsider. Pooling?
twist.a: No — transitory; apply the acquisition method.

Gaining control remeasures the old stake; losing control remeasures the retained stake — both through P&L.
Recognised in a combination even if not probable; Ind AS 37 would not.
Exchanged awards are modifications; post-combination part is remuneration.
